body.en:
A transistor is a three-terminal semiconductor device used for amplification (making a weak signal stronger) and switching (ON/OFF).

  • The word transistor comes from "transfer + resistor": it transfers a signal from a low-resistance input circuit to a high-resistance output circuit.
  • It was invented in 1947 at Bell Laboratories (USA) by John Bardeen, Walter Brattain and William Shockley, who received the Nobel Prize in 1956.
  • It replaced the bulky vacuum tube (triode) and started the era of modern electronics, ICs and computers.

Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT)

  • Bipolar: current is carried by both types of carriers – electrons and holes.
  • Junction: it has two P-N junctions.
  • Three terminals: Emitter (E), Base (B), Collector (C).
  • A BJT is a current-controlled device: a small base current controls a large collector current.

Advantages over vacuum tubes

Small size, light weight, no heater (instant start), low operating voltage, low power consumption, long life, rugged and cheap.
body.gu:
Transistor એ ત્રણ terminal વાળું semiconductor device છે, જે Amplification (નબળા signal ને મજબૂત બનાવવું) અને Switching (ON/OFF) માટે વપરાય છે.

  • Transistor શબ્દ "transfer + resistor" પરથી આવ્યો છે: તે signal ને ઓછા resistance વાળા input circuit થી વધુ resistance વાળા output circuit માં transfer કરે છે.
  • તેની શોધ 1947 માં Bell Laboratories (USA) માં John Bardeen, Walter Brattain અને William Shockley એ કરી હતી; તેમને 1956 માં Nobel Prize મળ્યું.
  • તેણે મોટી vacuum tube (triode) નું સ્થાન લીધું અને આધુનિક electronics, ICs અને computers ના યુગની શરૂઆત કરી.

Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT)

  • Bipolar: current બંને પ્રકારના carriers – electrons અને holes – દ્વારા વહન થાય છે.
  • Junction: તેમાં બે P-N junctions હોય છે.
  • ત્રણ terminals: Emitter (E), Base (B), Collector (C).
  • BJT એ current-controlled device છે: નાનો base current મોટા collector current ને નિયંત્રિત કરે છે.

Vacuum tubes કરતાં ફાયદા

નાનું કદ, ઓછું વજન, heater નહીં (તરત શરૂ), ઓછો operating voltage, ઓછો power વપરાશ, લાંબું આયુષ્ય, મજબૂત અને સસ્તું.

body.en:
A transistor is made by sandwiching a thin layer of one type of semiconductor between two layers of the opposite type. It has three regions and two junctions.

RegionDopingSizeFunction
Emitter (E)Heavily dopedMediumEmits (supplies) a large number of majority carriers into the base
Base (B)Lightly dopedVery thin (≈ 10⁻⁶ m)Controls the flow of carriers from emitter to collector
Collector (C)Moderately dopedLargestCollects carriers; large size to dissipate heat

Two junctions

  • Emitter-Base junction (JE) – between emitter and base.
  • Collector-Base junction (JC) – between collector and base.

So a transistor looks like two diodes connected back to back. But two separate diodes cannot work as a transistor, because the base must be very thin and lightly doped.

Why these doping levels and sizes?

  • Emitter heavily doped → it can inject a large number of carriers.
  • Base thin and lightly doped → very few carriers recombine in the base; most (95–99%) pass on to the collector.
  • Collector largest → most power is dissipated at the collector junction, so a large area is needed to remove heat.
  • Emitter and collector are the same type of material but cannot be interchanged, because their doping and size are different.

તેથી transistor પીઠ-પીઠ જોડેલા બે diodes જેવો દેખાય છે. પરંતુ બે અલગ diodes transistor તરીકે કામ કરી શકતા નથી, કારણ કે base ખૂબ પાતળું અને ઓછું doped હોવું જોઈએ.

આવું doping અને કદ કેમ?

  • Emitter વધુ doped → તે મોટી સંખ્યામાં carriers મોકલી શકે.
  • Base પાતળું અને ઓછું doped → base માં ખૂબ ઓછા carriers recombine થાય; મોટાભાગના (95–99%) collector સુધી પહોંચે.
  • Collector સૌથી મોટું → મોટાભાગનો power collector junction પર dissipate થાય છે, તેથી ઉષ્મા દૂર કરવા મોટો વિસ્તાર જોઈએ.
  • Emitter અને collector સમાન પ્રકારના material છે પરંતુ doping અને કદ અલગ હોવાથી તેમને અદલાબદલી કરી શકાતા નથી.

body.en:
1. NPN transistor

A thin P-type layer (base) is placed between two N-type layers (emitter and collector). Majority carriers are electrons.

2. PNP transistor

A thin N-type layer (base) is placed between two P-type layers. Majority carriers are holes.

Symbols

  • The arrow is always on the emitter and shows the direction of conventional current.
  • NPN: arrow points outward (Not Pointing iN). Current flows into C and B and out of E.
  • PNP: arrow points inward (Pointing iN Permanently). Current flows into E and out of B and C.
  • In both: IE = IB + IC.

Comparison of NPN and PNP

PointNPNPNP
StructureP-layer between two N-layersN-layer between two P-layers
Majority carriersElectronsHoles
Arrow in symbolOutward (on emitter)Inward (on emitter)
Biasing (active)Collector +ve, emitter −veCollector −ve, emitter +ve
SpeedFaster (electron mobility is higher)Slower
UseMore popularLess used; complementary circuits
ExamplesBC547, 2N2222, 2N3055BC557, 2N2907, 2N2955

Why is NPN more popular? Electrons have higher mobility than holes, so NPN transistors are faster and give better high-frequency performance; also most circuits use a positive supply.

Packages

  • TO-92 (small plastic, e.g. BC547, 2N2222A) – low-power signal transistors.
  • TO-220 (with metal tab, e.g. TIP31, TIP122) – medium power; mounted on a heat sink.
  • TO-3 (metal can, e.g. 2N3055) – high power; case is the collector.

Pin identification

  • BC547/BC557: hold the flat face towards you, leads down → pins are C – B – E from left to right.
  • Pin order differs between types, so always check the datasheet.
  • Multimeter test (diode mode): base-emitter and base-collector junctions each show ≈ 0.6–0.7 V in one direction only. If the red probe on the base gives readings to both other pins → NPN; if the black probe on the base does → PNP. The B-E reading is slightly higher than B-C.

h.en: 4.2.1 Biasing of Transistor and Regions of Operation
h.gu: 4.2.1 Transistor નું Biasing અને Regions of Operation

body.en:
To work as an amplifier, a transistor must be biased so that:

  • Emitter-base junction (JE) → forward biased (low resistance)
  • Collector-base junction (JC) → reverse biased (high resistance)

Depending on the bias of the two junctions, a transistor has four regions of operation:

RegionJEJCBehaviour / Use
ActiveForwardReverseIC = β IB; used as an amplifier
SaturationForwardForwardMaximum IC, VCE ≈ 0.2 V; ON switch
Cut-offReverseReverseIC ≈ 0; OFF switch
Inverse activeReverseForwardE and C roles exchanged; very low gain; rarely used

Typical values for a silicon transistor in the active region: VBE ≈ 0.7 V (0.3 V for Ge).

  • Emitter-base junction (JE) → forward biased (ઓછો resistance)
  • Collector-base junction (JC) → reverse biased (વધુ resistance)

બંને junctions ના bias પ્રમાણે transistor ના ચાર regions of operation છે:

Active region માં silicon transistor માટે સામાન્ય મૂલ્ય: VBE ≈ 0.7 V (Ge માટે 0.3 V).

body.en:
Biasing: VEE forward biases JE (emitter N to −ve, base P to +ve); VCC reverse biases JC (collector N to +ve).

Working

  1. Because JE is forward biased, the large number of free electrons in the heavily doped N-type emitter are pushed into the base. This forms the emitter current IE.
  2. The base is very thin and lightly doped (few holes). So only a very small number of electrons (about 1–5%) recombine with holes in the base. These form the small base current IB.
  3. The remaining electrons (about 95–99%) diffuse across the thin base and reach the collector-base junction.
  4. JC is reverse biased, so its electric field attracts (sweeps) these electrons into the collector, where they are collected by the positive terminal of VCC. This forms the collector current IC.

Thus: IE = IB + IC, and IC is almost equal to IE.

Inside the NPN transistor current is carried mainly by electrons. In the external circuit, conventional current flows into the collector and base and out of the emitter.

Key idea: a small change in base current (or VBE) produces a large change in collector current – this is the basis of amplification.
body.gu:
Biasing: VEE એ JE ને forward bias કરે છે (emitter N ને −ve, base P ને +ve); VCC એ JC ને reverse bias કરે છે (collector N ને +ve).

કાર્ય

  1. JE forward biased હોવાથી, વધુ doped N-type emitter ના મોટી સંખ્યાના free electrons base માં ધકેલાય છે. તેનાથી Emitter current IE બને છે.
  2. Base ખૂબ પાતળું અને ઓછું doped (ઓછા holes) છે. તેથી ફક્ત ખૂબ ઓછા electrons (આશરે 1–5%) base માં holes સાથે recombine થાય છે. તેનાથી નાનો Base current IB બને છે.
  3. બાકીના electrons (આશરે 95–99%) પાતળા base માંથી diffuse થઈ collector-base junction સુધી પહોંચે છે.
  4. JC reverse biased છે, તેથી તેનું electric field આ electrons ને collector માં ખેંચી લે છે, જ્યાં VCC નો positive terminal તેમને એકત્ર કરે છે. તેનાથી Collector current IC બને છે.

આમ: IE = IB + IC, અને IC લગભગ IE જેટલો હોય છે.

NPN transistor ની અંદર current મુખ્યત્વે electrons દ્વારા વહન થાય છે. બાહ્ય circuit માં conventional current collector અને base માં અંદર જાય છે અને emitter માંથી બહાર આવે છે.

મુખ્ય વિચાર: base current (અથવા VBE) માં નાનો ફેરફાર collector current માં મોટો ફેરફાર કરે છે – આ જ Amplification નો આધાર છે.

body.en:
Biasing: VEE forward biases JE (emitter P to +ve, base N to −ve); VCC reverse biases JC (collector P to −ve). All polarities are opposite to NPN.

Working

  1. JE is forward biased, so a large number of holes from the heavily doped P-type emitter are pushed into the N-type base → emitter current IE.
  2. The base is thin and lightly doped (few electrons), so only about 1–5% of holes recombine with electrons in the base → small base current IB.
  3. The remaining 95–99% of holes cross the base and reach JC.
  4. The reverse-biased JC (collector connected to −ve) attracts these holes into the collector → collector current IC.

Again IE = IB + IC. Inside the PNP transistor current is carried mainly by holes; in the external circuit, conventional current flows into the emitter and out of the base and collector.

Difference in working (NPN vs PNP)

  • NPN: majority carriers = electrons, collector +ve.
  • PNP: majority carriers = holes, collector −ve.
  • Both have the same current relations and the same principle of operation.

કાર્ય

  1. JE forward biased છે, તેથી વધુ doped P-type emitter ના મોટી સંખ્યાના holes N-type base માં ધકેલાય છે → Emitter current IE.
  2. Base પાતળું અને ઓછું doped (ઓછા electrons) છે, તેથી ફક્ત આશરે 1–5% holes base માં electrons સાથે recombine થાય છે → નાનો Base current IB.
  3. બાકીના 95–99% holes base પાર કરી JC સુધી પહોંચે છે.
  4. Reverse-biased JC (collector −ve સાથે) આ holes ને collector માં ખેંચે છે → Collector current IC.

ફરીથી IE = IB + IC. PNP transistor ની અંદર current મુખ્યત્વે holes દ્વારા વહન થાય છે; બાહ્ય circuit માં conventional current emitter માં અંદર જાય છે અને base અને collector માંથી બહાર આવે છે.

કાર્યમાં તફાવત (NPN અને PNP)

  • NPN: majority carriers = electrons, collector +ve.
  • PNP: majority carriers = holes, collector −ve.
  • બંનેમાં current સંબંધો અને કાર્ય સિદ્ધાંત સમાન છે.

body.en:
Basic current equation (KCL)

IE = IB + IC   (IB is very small, so IC ≈ IE)

α (alpha) – common-base DC current gain

α = IC / IE → always less than 1; typical 0.95 to 0.995.

β (beta) – common-emitter DC current gain (hFE)

β = IC / IB → large; typical 20 to 500.

Relation between α and β

Dividing IE = IB + IC by IC:   1/α = 1/β + 1

β = α / (1 − α)    and    α = β / (1 + β)

Example: α = 0.98 → β = 0.98/0.02 = 49. A small change in α causes a large change in β.

Leakage currents

  • ICBO: collector-base leakage current with emitter open (due to minority carriers in reverse-biased JC). nA for Si, µA for Ge. Doubles every 10 °C.
  • In CB: IC = α IE + ICBO
  • ICEO: collector-emitter leakage with base open: ICEO = (1 + β) ICBO (much larger).
  • In CE: IC = β IB + ICEO

Leakage current increases with temperature and can lead to thermal runaway if the circuit is not stabilised.
body.gu:
મૂળભૂત current સમીકરણ (KCL)

IE = IB + IC   (IB ખૂબ નાનો છે, તેથી IC ≈ IE)

α (alpha) – common-base DC current gain

α = IC / IE → હંમેશા 1 થી ઓછો; સામાન્ય 0.95 થી 0.995.

β (beta) – common-emitter DC current gain (hFE)

β = IC / IB → મોટો; સામાન્ય 20 થી 500.

α અને β વચ્ચેનો સંબંધ

IE = IB + IC ને IC વડે ભાગતાં:   1/α = 1/β + 1

β = α / (1 − α)    અને    α = β / (1 + β)

ઉદાહરણ: α = 0.98 → β = 0.98/0.02 = 49. α માં નાનો ફેરફાર β માં મોટો ફેરફાર કરે છે.

Leakage currents

  • ICBO: emitter open હોય ત્યારે collector-base leakage current (reverse-biased JC માં minority carriers ને કારણે). Si માટે nA, Ge માટે µA. દર 10 °C એ બમણો.
  • CB માં: IC = α IE + ICBO
  • ICEO: base open હોય ત્યારે collector-emitter leakage: ICEO = (1 + β) ICBO (ઘણો મોટો).
  • CE માં: IC = β IB + ICEO

Leakage current તાપમાન સાથે વધે છે અને circuit stabilise ન હોય તો Thermal runaway થઈ શકે છે.

body.en:
• Active region (amplifier): JE forward, JC reverse.
  • Saturation: both forward (ON switch); Cut-off: both reverse (OFF switch).
  • Emitter injects carriers; only 1–5% recombine in thin base (IB); 95–99% reach collector (IC).
  • NPN: electrons; PNP: holes; supply polarities opposite.
  • IE = IB + IC; α = IC/IE (< 1); β = IC/IB (20–500).
  • β = α/(1 − α), α = β/(1 + β).
  • ICEO = (1 + β) ICBO; IC = β IB + ICEO.
body.gu:
• Active region (amplifier): JE forward, JC reverse.
  • Saturation: બંને forward (ON switch); Cut-off: બંને reverse (OFF switch).
  • Emitter carriers મોકલે; પાતળા base માં ફક્ત 1–5% recombine (IB); 95–99% collector સુધી (IC).
  • NPN: electrons; PNP: holes; supply polarities વિરુદ્ધ.
  • IE = IB + IC; α = IC/IE (< 1); β = IC/IB (20–500).
  • β = α/(1 − α), α = β/(1 + β).
  • ICEO = (1 + β) ICBO; IC = β IB + ICEO.

body.en:
A transistor has three terminals, but a circuit needs four terminals – two for input and two for output. So one terminal is made common to both the input and the output circuits.

Depending on which terminal is common, there are three configurations (connections):

ConfigurationCommon terminalInput betweenOutput between
Common Base (CB)BaseEmitter – BaseCollector – Base
Common Emitter (CE)EmitterBase – EmitterCollector – Emitter
Common Collector (CC)CollectorBase – CollectorEmitter – Collector

In every configuration, for amplifier operation, the emitter-base junction is forward biased and the collector-base junction is reverse biased.

Characteristics

Graphs that show the relation between currents and voltages of a transistor are called characteristics:

  • Input characteristics: input current vs input voltage, with output voltage constant.
  • Output characteristics: output current vs output voltage, with input current constant.
body.gu:
Transistor માં ત્રણ terminals છે, પરંતુ circuit ને ચાર terminals જોઈએ – બે input માટે અને બે output માટે. તેથી એક terminal ને input અને output બંને circuits માટે common બનાવાય છે.

કયો terminal common છે તેના આધારે ત્રણ configurations (જોડાણ) છે:

ConfigurationCommon terminalInput વચ્ચેOutput વચ્ચે
Common Base (CB)BaseEmitter – BaseCollector – Base
Common Emitter (CE)EmitterBase – EmitterCollector – Emitter
Common Collector (CC)CollectorBase – CollectorEmitter – Collector

દરેક configuration માં amplifier કાર્ય માટે emitter-base junction forward biased અને collector-base junction reverse biased હોય છે.

Characteristics

Transistor ના currents અને voltages વચ્ચેનો સંબંધ બતાવતા આલેખોને Characteristics કહે છે:

  • Input characteristics: output voltage અચળ રાખી input current વિરુદ્ધ input voltage.
  • Output characteristics: input current અચળ રાખી output current વિરુદ્ધ output voltage.

body.en:
In CB configuration the base is common to input and output. Input is applied between emitter and base, and output is taken between collector and base (see diagram for NPN).

  • VEE forward biases the emitter-base junction; VCC reverse biases the collector-base junction.
  • Input current = IE; output current = IC.

Current amplification factor (α)

α = ΔIC / ΔIE (VCB constant) → less than 1 (0.95–0.995). So CB gives no current gain.

Features

  • Current gain: less than 1 (α)
  • Voltage gain: high (because output resistance ≫ input resistance)
  • Input resistance: very low (≈ 20 – 100 Ω)
  • Output resistance: very high (≈ 500 kΩ – 1 MΩ)
  • Phase shift between input and output: 0° (in phase)
  • Application: high-frequency (RF) amplifiers, impedance matching from low to high impedance
body.gu:
CB configuration માં base input અને output માટે common છે. Input emitter અને base વચ્ચે લગાવાય છે અને output collector અને base વચ્ચેથી લેવાય છે (NPN માટે આકૃતિ જુઓ).

  • VEE emitter-base junction ને forward bias કરે; VCC collector-base junction ને reverse bias કરે.
  • Input current = IE; output current = IC.

Current amplification factor (α)

α = ΔIC / ΔIE (VCB અચળ) → 1 થી ઓછો (0.95–0.995). તેથી CB માં current gain મળતો નથી.

લક્ષણો

  • Current gain: 1 થી ઓછો (α)
  • Voltage gain: વધુ (કારણ કે output resistance ≫ input resistance)
  • Input resistance: ખૂબ ઓછો (≈ 20 – 100 Ω)
  • Output resistance: ખૂબ વધુ (≈ 500 kΩ – 1 MΩ)
  • Input અને output વચ્ચે phase shift: 0° (in phase)
  • ઉપયોગ: High-frequency (RF) amplifiers, ઓછા થી વધુ impedance સુધી impedance matching

body.en:
Input characteristics (IE vs VEB, VCB constant)

  • The curve is like the forward characteristic of a diode (emitter-base junction is forward biased).
  • Emitter current is very small until VEB reaches the knee voltage (≈ 0.7 V for Si), then it rises rapidly.
  • When VCB is increased, the curve shifts slightly left (more IE for the same VEB) due to the Early effect (base-width modulation).
  • Input resistance ri = ΔVEB / ΔIE → very low (tens of ohms).

Output characteristics (IC vs VCB, IE constant)

  • Active region: IC ≈ IE and is almost independent of VCB → the curves are nearly flat (horizontal) lines.
  • Even at VCB = 0, IC flows. To reduce IC to zero, the collector-base junction must be slightly forward biased (negative VCB) → saturation region.
  • Cut-off region: below the IE = 0 curve; only ICBO flows.
  • Output resistance ro = ΔVCB / ΔIC → very high (since the curves are almost flat).
body.gu:
Input characteristics (IE વિરુદ્ધ VEB, VCB અચળ)

  • Curve diode ની forward characteristic જેવો છે (emitter-base junction forward biased છે).
  • VEB knee voltage (Si માટે ≈ 0.7 V) સુધી પહોંચે ત્યાં સુધી emitter current ખૂબ નાનો રહે છે, પછી ઝડપથી વધે છે.
  • VCB વધારતાં Early effect (base-width modulation) ને કારણે curve થોડો ડાબી તરફ ખસે છે (સમાન VEB માટે વધુ IE).
  • Input resistance ri = ΔVEB / ΔIE → ખૂબ ઓછો (દસેક ohms).

Output characteristics (IC વિરુદ્ધ VCB, IE અચળ)

  • Active region: IC ≈ IE અને લગભગ VCB થી સ્વતંત્ર → curves લગભગ સપાટ (આડી) રેખાઓ છે.
  • VCB = 0 પર પણ IC વહે છે. IC ને શૂન્ય કરવા collector-base junction ને થોડો forward bias (negative VCB) કરવો પડે → Saturation region.
  • Cut-off region: IE = 0 curve ની નીચે; ફક્ત ICBO વહે.
  • Output resistance ro = ΔVCB / ΔIC → ખૂબ વધુ (curves લગભગ સપાટ હોવાથી).

body.en:
In CE configuration the emitter is common to input and output. Input is applied between base and emitter, and output is taken between collector and emitter (see diagram).

  • VBB (through RB) forward biases the base-emitter junction; VCC (through RC) keeps the collector-base junction reverse biased (VCC > VBB).
  • Input current = IB; output current = IC.

Current amplification factor (β)

β = ΔIC / ΔIB (VCE constant) → large (20–500). So CE gives high current gain.

Features

  • Current gain: high (β)
  • Voltage gain: high (≈ 100–500)
  • Power gain: highest of all three
  • Input resistance: medium (≈ 1 kΩ)
  • Output resistance: medium (≈ 10 – 50 kΩ)
  • Phase shift: 180° (output is inverted)
  • Application: audio amplifiers, voltage amplifiers, switching; the most widely used configuration
body.gu:
CE configuration માં emitter input અને output માટે common છે. Input base અને emitter વચ્ચે લગાવાય છે અને output collector અને emitter વચ્ચેથી લેવાય છે (આકૃતિ જુઓ).

  • VBB (RB દ્વારા) base-emitter junction ને forward bias કરે; VCC (RC દ્વારા) collector-base junction ને reverse biased રાખે (VCC > VBB).
  • Input current = IB; output current = IC.

Current amplification factor (β)

β = ΔIC / ΔIB (VCE અચળ) → મોટો (20–500). તેથી CE માં વધુ current gain મળે છે.

લક્ષણો

  • Current gain: વધુ (β)
  • Voltage gain: વધુ (≈ 100–500)
  • Power gain: ત્રણેયમાં સૌથી વધુ
  • Input resistance: મધ્યમ (≈ 1 kΩ)
  • Output resistance: મધ્યમ (≈ 10 – 50 kΩ)
  • Phase shift: 180° (output ઉલટો)
  • ઉપયોગ: Audio amplifiers, voltage amplifiers, switching; સૌથી વધુ વપરાતું configuration

body.en:
The characteristics of an NPN transistor in CE configuration are obtained with the circuit shown.

Components

  • VBB – variable DC supply for the base circuit, with series resistor RB.
  • Micro-ammeter (µA) – measures base current IB.
  • Voltmeter across B-E – measures VBE.
  • VCC – variable DC supply for the collector circuit.
  • Milli-ammeter (mA) – measures collector current IC.
  • Voltmeter across C-E – measures VCE.

Procedure

  1. Input characteristics: keep VCE constant (e.g. 1 V). Vary VBB in small steps and note VBE and IB. Repeat for VCE = 5 V. Plot IB vs VBE.
  2. Output characteristics: set IB to a fixed value (e.g. 20 µA) using VBB. Vary VCC and note VCE and IC. Repeat for IB = 40, 60, 80 µA. Plot IC vs VCE.
body.gu:
CE configuration માં NPN transistor ની characteristics આકૃતિમાં બતાવેલ circuit થી મેળવાય છે.

ઘટકો

  • VBB – base circuit માટે variable DC supply, series resistor RB સાથે.
  • Micro-ammeter (µA) – base current IB માપે.
  • B-E પર Voltmeter – VBE માપે.
  • VCC – collector circuit માટે variable DC supply.
  • Milli-ammeter (mA) – collector current IC માપે.
  • C-E પર Voltmeter – VCE માપે.

પદ્ધતિ

  1. Input characteristics: VCE અચળ રાખો (દા.ત. 1 V). VBB નાના પગલાંમાં બદલો અને VBE અને IB નોંધો. VCE = 5 V માટે ફરી કરો. IB વિરુદ્ધ VBE નો આલેખ દોરો.
  2. Output characteristics: VBB થી IB ને નિશ્ચિત મૂલ્ય (દા.ત. 20 µA) પર રાખો. VCC બદલો અને VCE અને IC નોંધો. IB = 40, 60, 80 µA માટે ફરી કરો. IC વિરુદ્ધ VCE નો આલેખ દોરો.

body.en:
Definition: The curve between base current IB and base-emitter voltage VBE at constant VCE.

Observations

  1. The curve is similar to the forward characteristic of a P-N diode, because the base-emitter junction is forward biased.
  2. IB is almost zero until VBE reaches the knee voltage (≈ 0.7 V for Si, 0.3 V for Ge). After that IB rises rapidly.
  3. IB is in micro-amperes (µA).
  4. When VCE is increased, the curve shifts slightly to the right (less IB for the same VBE). This is due to the Early effect: higher VCE widens the collector-base depletion layer, the effective base width decreases, fewer carriers recombine in the base, so IB decreases.

Input resistance

ri = ΔVBE / ΔIB (VCE constant) → medium, about 1 kΩ (higher than CB).
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા: અચળ VCE પર base current IB અને base-emitter voltage VBE વચ્ચેનો curve.

અવલોકનો

  1. Base-emitter junction forward biased હોવાથી curve P-N diode ની forward characteristic જેવો છે.
  2. VBE એ knee voltage (Si માટે ≈ 0.7 V, Ge માટે 0.3 V) સુધી પહોંચે ત્યાં સુધી IB લગભગ શૂન્ય રહે છે. પછી IB ઝડપથી વધે છે.
  3. IB micro-amperes (µA) માં હોય છે.
  4. VCE વધારતાં curve થોડો જમણી તરફ ખસે છે (સમાન VBE માટે ઓછો IB). આ Early effect ને કારણે છે: વધુ VCE collector-base depletion layer ને પહોળું કરે છે, અસરકારક base width ઘટે છે, base માં ઓછા carriers recombine થાય છે, તેથી IB ઘટે છે.

Input resistance

ri = ΔVBE / ΔIB (VCE અચળ) → મધ્યમ, આશરે 1 kΩ (CB કરતાં વધુ).

body.en:
Definition: The curves between collector current IC and collector-emitter voltage VCE for different constant values of IB.

Observations

  1. For a fixed IB, as VCE increases from 0, IC rises rapidly at first (up to about 0.2–1 V).
  2. After that, IC becomes almost constant and depends mainly on IB (IC ≈ β IB). The curve rises only slightly due to the Early effect.
  3. Higher IB → higher curve. Equal steps of IB give nearly equal steps of IC.

Three regions

RegionWhere on graphJunctionsUse
ActiveFlat middle part of curvesJE FB, JC RBAmplifier (IC = β IB)
SaturationSteep part near the IC axis (VCE < ≈ 0.2 V)Both FBON switch
Cut-offBelow the IB = 0 curveBoth RBOFF switch (only ICEO flows)

Parameters

  • Output resistance ro = ΔVCE / ΔIC (IB constant) → medium (10–50 kΩ).
  • AC current gain β = ΔIC / ΔIB (VCE constant) – can be found from two curves.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા: IB ના જુદા જુદા અચળ મૂલ્યો માટે collector current IC અને collector-emitter voltage VCE વચ્ચેના curves.

અવલોકનો

  1. નિશ્ચિત IB માટે VCE ને 0 થી વધારતાં, શરૂઆતમાં (આશરે 0.2–1 V સુધી) IC ઝડપથી વધે છે.
  2. પછી IC લગભગ અચળ બને છે અને મુખ્યત્વે IB પર આધાર રાખે છે (IC ≈ β IB). Early effect ને કારણે curve થોડો જ વધે છે.
  3. વધુ IB → ઉંચો curve. IB ના સમાન પગલાં IC ના લગભગ સમાન પગલાં આપે.

ત્રણ regions

Regionઆલેખ પર ક્યાંJunctionsઉપયોગ
ActiveCurves નો સપાટ મધ્ય ભાગJE FB, JC RBAmplifier (IC = β IB)
SaturationIC axis નજીકનો ઊભો ભાગ (VCE < ≈ 0.2 V)બંને FBON switch
Cut-offIB = 0 curve ની નીચેબંને RBOFF switch (ફક્ત ICEO વહે)

Parameters

  • Output resistance ro = ΔVCE / ΔIC (IB અચળ) → મધ્યમ (10–50 kΩ).
  • AC current gain β = ΔIC / ΔIB (VCE અચળ) – બે curves પરથી શોધી શકાય.

body.en:
In CC configuration the collector is common to input and output. Input is applied between base and collector, and output is taken across the emitter resistor, between emitter and collector (see diagram). The collector is common through VCC (AC ground).

  • Input current = IB; output current = IE.
  • It is also called an emitter follower, because the output (emitter) voltage follows the input (base) voltage: Vout ≈ Vin − 0.7 V.

Current amplification factor (γ)

γ = ΔIE / ΔIB = 1 + β → highest current gain.

Features

  • Current gain: highest (1 + β)
  • Voltage gain: less than 1 (≈ 1)
  • Power gain: low (≈ γ)
  • Input resistance: very high (≈ 100 kΩ – 1 MΩ)
  • Output resistance: very low (≈ 10 – 100 Ω)
  • Phase shift: 0°
  • Application: buffer amplifier, impedance matching (high to low impedance), driving low-impedance loads such as speakers
body.gu:
CC configuration માં collector input અને output માટે common છે. Input base અને collector વચ્ચે લગાવાય છે અને output emitter resistor પરથી, emitter અને collector વચ્ચેથી લેવાય છે (આકૃતિ જુઓ). Collector, VCC (AC ground) દ્વારા common છે.

  • Input current = IB; output current = IE.
  • તેને Emitter follower પણ કહે છે, કારણ કે output (emitter) voltage input (base) voltage ને અનુસરે છે: Vout ≈ Vin − 0.7 V.

Current amplification factor (γ)

γ = ΔIE / ΔIB = 1 + β → સૌથી વધુ current gain.

લક્ષણો

  • Current gain: સૌથી વધુ (1 + β)
  • Voltage gain: 1 થી ઓછો (≈ 1)
  • Power gain: ઓછો (≈ γ)
  • Input resistance: ખૂબ વધુ (≈ 100 kΩ – 1 MΩ)
  • Output resistance: ખૂબ ઓછો (≈ 10 – 100 Ω)
  • Phase shift: 0°
  • ઉપયોગ: Buffer amplifier, Impedance matching (વધુ થી ઓછા impedance સુધી), speakers જેવા ઓછા impedance વાળા loads ચલાવવા

h.en: 4.4.1 Current Gain (α, β, γ) and Their Relations
h.gu: 4.4.1 Current Gain (α, β, γ) અને તેમના સંબંધો

body.en:
Current gain = output current / input current. It has no unit.

GainConfigurationFormulaTypical value
α (alpha)CBα = IC / IE0.95 – 0.995 (< 1)
β (beta, hFE)CEβ = IC / IB20 – 500
γ (gamma)CCγ = IE / IB21 – 501 (= 1 + β)

DC gain uses DC values (e.g. βdc = hFE = IC/IB); AC gain uses small changes (βac = hfe = ΔIC/ΔIB). In basic problems they are taken as equal.

Derivation of relations

Start with IE = IB + IC.

(1) β in terms of α: β = IC/IB = IC/(IE − IC). Divide numerator and denominator by IE:

β = (IC/IE) / (1 − IC/IE) → β = α / (1 − α)

(2) α in terms of β: α = IC/IE = IC/(IB + IC). Divide by IB:

α = β / (1 + β) → α = β / (1 + β)

(3) γ in terms of β: γ = IE/IB = (IB + IC)/IB → γ = 1 + β

(4) γ in terms of α: γ = 1 + α/(1 − α) → γ = 1 / (1 − α)

As α → 1, β becomes very large: α = 0.99 → β = 99; α = 0.995 → β = 199.
body.gu:
Current gain = output current / input current. તેનો કોઈ એકમ નથી.

GainConfigurationસૂત્રસામાન્ય મૂલ્ય

β (beta, hFE)CEβ = IC / IB20 – 500
γ (gamma)CCγ = IE / IB21 – 501 (= 1 + β)

DC gain માં DC મૂલ્યો વપરાય (દા.ત. βdc = hFE = IC/IB); AC gain માં નાના ફેરફારો વપરાય (βac = hfe = ΔIC/ΔIB). સામાન્ય દાખલાઓમાં બંને સમાન લેવાય છે.

સંબંધોની સાબિતી (Derivation)

IE = IB + IC થી શરૂ કરો.

(1) α ના રૂપમાં β: β = IC/IB = IC/(IE − IC). અંશ અને છેદ ને IE વડે ભાગો:

β = (IC/IE) / (1 − IC/IE) → β = α / (1 − α)

(2) β ના રૂપમાં α: α = IC/IE = IC/(IB + IC). IB વડે ભાગો:

α = β / (1 + β) → α = β / (1 + β)

(3) β ના રૂપમાં γ: γ = IE/IB = (IB + IC)/IB → γ = 1 + β

(4) α ના રૂપમાં γ: γ = 1 + α/(1 − α) → γ = 1 / (1 − α)

α → 1 થાય તેમ β ખૂબ મોટો બને: α = 0.99 → β = 99; α = 0.995 → β = 199.

body.en:
Voltage gain (Av)

Av = output voltage / input voltage = ΔVout / ΔVin

Output voltage = output current × load resistance (RL); input voltage = input current × input resistance (ri).

ConfigurationVoltage gainRemark
CBAv = α × RL / riHigh, because RL ≫ ri
CEAv = β × RL / riHigh; output inverted (−)
CCAv ≈ 1 (slightly less)Output follows input

Even though α < 1 in CB, voltage gain is high because the output resistance (load) is much larger than the input resistance. That is why the device is called a trans-resistor.

Power gain (Ap)

Ap = output power / input power = current gain × voltage gain

  • CB: Ap = α × Av (medium)
  • CE: Ap = β × Av = β² RL / ri (highest)
  • CC: Ap ≈ γ (low)

Gain in decibels

Power gain (dB) = 10 log10 Ap; voltage gain (dB) = 20 log10 Av.

h.en: 4.5.1 DC Load Line and Regions for Switching
h.gu: 4.5.1 DC Load Line અને Switching માટેના Regions

body.en:
In a CE circuit, applying KVL to the collector loop:

VCE = VCC − IC RC

This is the equation of a straight line called the DC load line. It is drawn on the output characteristics using two points:

  • Cut-off point (IC = 0): VCE = VCC
  • Saturation point (VCE ≈ 0): IC(sat) = VCC / RC

The operating point (Q-point) of the transistor always lies on this load line.

Use of the regions

  • Amplifier: Q-point in the middle of the load line (active region).
  • Switch: the transistor is operated only at the two ends of the load line – cut-off (OFF) and saturation (ON). It moves quickly between them and does not stay in the active region.
body.gu:
CE circuit માં collector loop પર KVL લગાવતાં:

VCE = VCC − IC RC

આ એક સીધી રેખાનું સમીકરણ છે જેને DC load line કહે છે. તે output characteristics પર બે બિંદુઓથી દોરાય છે:

  • Cut-off બિંદુ (IC = 0): VCE = VCC
  • Saturation બિંદુ (VCE ≈ 0): IC(sat) = VCC / RC

Transistor નું operating point (Q-point) હંમેશા આ load line પર જ હોય છે.

Regions નો ઉપયોગ

  • Amplifier: Q-point load line ના મધ્યમાં (active region).
  • Switch: transistor ફક્ત load line ના બે છેડે ચલાવાય છે – cut-off (OFF) અને saturation (ON). તે તેમની વચ્ચે ઝડપથી બદલાય છે અને active region માં રહેતો નથી.

h.en: 4.5.2 Working of Transistor as a Switch

body.en:
Circuit: An NPN transistor in CE configuration. The load (LED, lamp, relay) with RC is connected between +VCC and the collector; the emitter is grounded; the input Vin is applied to the base through RB (see diagram).

1. Switch OFF – Cut-off region (Vin = 0 / LOW)

  • VBE < 0.7 V → both junctions reverse biased.
  • IB = 0, so IC ≈ 0 (only tiny leakage).
  • No voltage drop across RC, so VCE ≈ VCC.
  • The transistor behaves like an open switch between C and E → load (LED) is OFF.

2. Switch ON – Saturation region (Vin = HIGH)

  • Large base current flows, both junctions become forward biased.
  • IC reaches its maximum: IC(sat) = (VCC − VCE(sat)) / RC ≈ VCC / RC.
  • VCE(sat) ≈ 0.2 V (almost zero).
  • The transistor behaves like a closed switch → load (LED) is ON.

Condition for saturation

IB > IC(sat) / β. In practice IB is taken 2–10 times this value to make sure the transistor is fully ON (hard saturation).

Base resistor: RB = (Vin − VBE) / IB

Transistor switch as an inverter (NOT gate)

Input LOW → output (VCE) HIGH; input HIGH → output LOW. So the transistor switch acts as a NOT gate.

Vin0 (LOW)HIGH
JE, JCBoth reverseBoth forward
IC≈ 0IC(sat) ≈ VCC/RC
VCE≈ VCC≈ 0.2 V

body.gu:
Circuit: CE configuration માં NPN transistor. Load (LED, lamp, relay) RC સાથે +VCC અને collector વચ્ચે જોડાય છે; emitter ground થાય છે; input Vin RB દ્વારા base પર લગાવાય છે (આકૃતિ જુઓ).

1. Switch OFF – Cut-off region (Vin = 0 / LOW)

  • VBE < 0.7 V → બંને junctions reverse biased.
  • IB = 0, તેથી IC ≈ 0 (ફક્ત ખૂબ નાનો leakage).
  • RC પર કોઈ voltage drop નહીં, તેથી VCE ≈ VCC.
  • Transistor C અને E વચ્ચે ખુલ્લા switch જેવું વર્તે છે → load (LED) OFF.

2. Switch ON – Saturation region (Vin = HIGH)

  • મોટો base current વહે છે, બંને junctions forward biased થાય છે.
  • IC મહત્તમ થાય છે: IC(sat) = (VCC − VCE(sat)) / RC ≈ VCC / RC.
  • VCE(sat) ≈ 0.2 V (લગભગ શૂન્ય).
  • Transistor બંધ switch જેવું વર્તે છે → load (LED) ON.

Saturation માટેની શરત

IB > IC(sat) / β. વ્યવહારમાં transistor સંપૂર્ણ ON (hard saturation) થાય તે માટે IB આ મૂલ્ય કરતાં 2–10 ગણો લેવાય છે.

Base resistor: RB = (Vin − VBE) / IB

Inverter (NOT gate) તરીકે transistor switch

Input LOW → output (VCE) HIGH; input HIGH → output LOW. તેથી transistor switch NOT gate તરીકે કામ કરે છે.

h.en: 4.5.3 Applications and Advantages of Transistor Switch
h.gu: 4.5.3 Transistor Switch ના ઉપયોગો અને ફાયદા

body.en:
Applications

  • LED / lamp driver – microcontroller (Arduino) pins give small current; a transistor switches the larger load current.
  • Relay driver – switches a relay coil to control AC appliances (with a freewheeling diode across the coil).
  • Motor and buzzer control.
  • Digital logic circuits – NOT, NAND, NOR gates (TTL logic).
  • Automatic street light (with LDR), fire/water-level alarms, touch switches.
  • Switching power supplies (SMPS), inverters and PWM control.

Advantages over a mechanical switch

Moving partsNoneYes (wear and tear)
Switching speedVery fast (µs – ns)Slow (ms)
Sparking / bouncingNoYes
ControlElectronic (small signal)Manual
LifeVery longLimited
SizeVery smallLarger

Limitations: small voltage drop when ON (VCE(sat)), small leakage when OFF, limited current/voltage rating; it is used for DC loads (AC loads via relay/TRIAC).

ઉપયોગો

  • LED / lamp driver – microcontroller (Arduino) pins નાનો current આપે છે; transistor મોટો load current switch કરે છે.
  • Relay driver – AC appliances નિયંત્રિત કરવા relay coil ને switch કરે (coil પર freewheeling diode સાથે).
  • Motor અને buzzer નિયંત્રણ.
  • Digital logic circuits – NOT, NAND, NOR gates (TTL logic).
  • Automatic street light (LDR સાથે), fire/water-level alarms, touch switches.
  • Switching power supplies (SMPS), inverters અને PWM control.

મર્યાદાઓ: ON હોય ત્યારે નાનો voltage drop (VCE(sat)), OFF હોય ત્યારે નાનો leakage, મર્યાદિત current/voltage rating; DC loads માટે વપરાય (AC loads relay/TRIAC દ્વારા).

body.en:
• DC load line: VCE = VCC − ICRC; end points (VCC, 0) and (0, VCC/RC).
  • Amplifier → active region (middle); switch → cut-off and saturation (ends).
  • OFF: Vin LOW, IB = 0, IC ≈ 0, VCE ≈ VCC → open switch.
  • ON: Vin HIGH, IC = IC(sat), VCE ≈ 0.2 V → closed switch.
  • Saturation condition: IB > IC(sat)/β; RB = (Vin − 0.7)/IB.
  • Transistor switch = NOT gate; used for LED/relay/motor drivers; faster and longer-lasting than mechanical switches.

q.gu: Transistor માં I_CBO = 5 µA અને β = 100 છે. I_CEO શોધો. I_B = 20 µA હોય ત્યારે I_C પણ શોધો.

a.en:
ICEO = (1 + β) ICBO = 101 × 5 µA = 505 µA ≈ 0.505 mA

IC = β IB + ICEO = 100 × 20 µA + 0.505 mA = 2 + 0.505 = 2.505 mA

Leakage in CE is (1 + β) times larger than in CB.
a.gu:
ICEO = (1 + β) ICBO = 101 × 5 µA = 505 µA ≈ 0.505 mA

IC = β IB + ICEO = 100 × 20 µA + 0.505 mA = 2 + 0.505 = 2.505 mA

CE માં leakage, CB કરતાં (1 + β) ગણો વધુ હોય છે.

q.en: In a CE circuit, V_CC = 12 V and R_C = 2 kΩ. Find the end points of the DC load line. If I_B = 30 µA and β = 100, find the Q-point.
q.gu: CE circuit માં V_CC = 12 V અને R_C = 2 kΩ છે. DC load line ના છેડાના બિંદુઓ શોધો. જો I_B = 30 µA અને β = 100 હોય તો Q-point શોધો.

a.en:
Cut-off point: IC = 0 → VCE = VCC = 12 V

Saturation point: VCE = 0 → IC(sat) = VCC / RC = 12 / 2000 = 6 mA

Q-point: IC = β IB = 100 × 30 µA = 3 mA

VCE = VCC − IC RC = 12 − 3 × 2 = 6 V

Q-point = (6 V, 3 mA) – exactly in the middle of the load line → good for an amplifier.
a.gu:
Cut-off બિંદુ: IC = 0 → VCE = VCC = 12 V

Saturation બિંદુ: VCE = 0 → IC(sat) = VCC / RC = 12 / 2000 = 6 mA

Q-point: IC = β IB = 100 × 30 µA = 3 mA

VCE = VCC − IC RC = 12 − 3 × 2 = 6 V

Q-point = (6 V, 3 mA) – load line ના બરાબર મધ્યમાં → amplifier માટે યોગ્ય.

q.en: What is a transistor?
q.gu: Transistor એટલે શું?

a.en: A three-terminal semiconductor device used for amplification and switching.
a.gu: Amplification અને switching માટે વપરાતું ત્રણ terminal વાળું semiconductor device.

q.en: Why is it called 'bipolar'?
q.gu: તેને 'bipolar' કેમ કહે છે?

a.en: Because both electrons and holes take part in conduction.
a.gu: કારણ કે conduction માં electrons અને holes બંને ભાગ લે છે.

q.en: Name the three terminals of a BJT.
q.gu: BJT ના ત્રણ terminals ના નામ આપો.

a.en: Emitter, Base and Collector.
a.gu: Emitter, Base અને Collector.

q.en: Which region is most heavily doped?
q.gu: કયો region સૌથી વધુ doped છે?

a.en: Emitter.
a.gu: Emitter.

q.en: Why is the base made thin and lightly doped?
q.gu: Base ને પાતળો અને ઓછો doped કેમ બનાવાય છે?

a.en: So that very few carriers recombine in the base and most reach the collector.
a.gu: જેથી base માં ખૂબ ઓછા carriers recombine થાય અને મોટાભાગના collector સુધી પહોંચે.

q.en: Why is the collector made largest?
q.gu: Collector ને સૌથી મોટો કેમ બનાવાય છે?

a.en: To dissipate the heat produced at the collector junction.
a.gu: Collector junction પર ઉત્પન્ન થતી ઉષ્મા દૂર કરવા.

q.en: Can emitter and collector be interchanged?
q.gu: Emitter અને collector અદલાબદલી કરી શકાય?

a.en: No, because their doping levels and sizes are different.
a.gu: ના, કારણ કે તેમના doping અને કદ અલગ છે.

q.en: How do you identify NPN and PNP from the symbol?
q.gu: Symbol પરથી NPN અને PNP કેવી રીતે ઓળખાય?

a.en: NPN: emitter arrow points outward; PNP: arrow points inward.
a.gu: NPN: emitter arrow બહાર તરફ; PNP: arrow અંદર તરફ.

q.en: What biasing is needed for the active region?
q.gu: Active region માટે કયું biasing જરૂરી છે?

a.en: Emitter-base junction forward biased and collector-base junction reverse biased.
a.gu: Emitter-base junction forward biased અને collector-base junction reverse biased.

q.en: What percentage of emitter current reaches the collector?
q.gu: Emitter current ના કેટલા ટકા collector સુધી પહોંચે છે?

a.en: About 95–99%.

q.en: Why is NPN preferred over PNP?
q.gu: PNP કરતાં NPN કેમ વધુ પસંદ કરાય છે?

a.en: Electrons have higher mobility than holes, so NPN is faster.
a.gu: Electrons ની mobility holes કરતાં વધુ છે, તેથી NPN વધુ ઝડપી છે.

q.en: Pin order of BC547 (flat face towards you)?
q.gu: BC547 નો pin ક્રમ (સપાટ ભાગ તમારી તરફ)?

a.en: Collector – Base – Emitter (left to right).
a.gu: Collector – Base – Emitter (ડાબેથી જમણે).

q.en: Name the three transistor configurations.
q.gu: Transistor ના ત્રણ configurations ના નામ આપો.

a.en: Common Base (CB), Common Emitter (CE) and Common Collector (CC).
a.gu: Common Base (CB), Common Emitter (CE) અને Common Collector (CC).

q.en: Which configuration is most widely used and why?
q.gu: કયું configuration સૌથી વધુ વપરાય છે અને કેમ?

a.en: CE, because it gives the highest power gain with good current and voltage gain.
a.gu: CE, કારણ કે તે સારા current અને voltage gain સાથે સૌથી વધુ power gain આપે છે.

q.en: Define α.
q.gu: α ની વ્યાખ્યા આપો.

a.en: Ratio of collector current to emitter current (I_C/I_E) in CB.
a.gu: CB માં collector current અને emitter current નો ગુણોત્તર (I_C/I_E).

q.en: Define β.
q.gu: β ની વ્યાખ્યા આપો.

a.en: Ratio of collector current to base current (I_C/I_B) in CE.
a.gu: CE માં collector current અને base current નો ગુણોત્તર (I_C/I_B).

q.en: Relation between α and β?
q.gu: α અને β વચ્ચેનો સંબંધ?

a.en: β = α/(1 − α) and α = β/(1 + β).

q.en: What is γ?
q.gu: γ એટલે શું?

a.en: Current gain of CC configuration: γ = I_E/I_B = 1 + β.
a.gu: CC configuration નો current gain: γ = I_E/I_B = 1 + β.

q.en: Which configuration has the highest input resistance?
q.gu: કયા configuration માં સૌથી વધુ input resistance છે?

a.en: Common Collector (CC).
a.gu: Common Collector (CC).

q.en: Which configuration has phase shift of 180°?
q.gu: કયા configuration માં 180° phase shift છે?

a.en: Common Emitter (CE).
a.gu: Common Emitter (CE).

q.en: Why is CC called an emitter follower?
q.gu: CC ને emitter follower કેમ કહે છે?

a.en: Because the emitter (output) voltage follows the base (input) voltage; voltage gain ≈ 1.
a.gu: કારણ કે emitter (output) voltage base (input) voltage ને અનુસરે છે; voltage gain ≈ 1.

q.en: What is the Early effect?
q.gu: Early effect એટલે શું?

a.en: Reduction of effective base width when collector voltage increases (base-width modulation).
a.gu: Collector voltage વધતાં અસરકારક base width ઘટવું (base-width modulation).

q.en: What are the regions on CE output characteristics?
q.gu: CE output characteristics પર કયા regions છે?

a.en: Active, saturation and cut-off regions.
a.gu: Active, saturation અને cut-off regions.

q.en: What is thermal runaway?
q.gu: Thermal runaway એટલે શું?

a.en: Self-heating cycle: temperature ↑ → leakage ↑ → I_C ↑ → more heat, which can destroy the transistor.
a.gu: સ્વ-ગરમીનું ચક્ર: તાપમાન ↑ → leakage ↑ → I_C ↑ → વધુ ઉષ્મા, જે transistor ને નષ્ટ કરી શકે.

q.en: In which regions does a transistor work as a switch?
q.gu: Transistor switch તરીકે કયા regions માં કામ કરે છે?

a.en: Cut-off (OFF) and saturation (ON).
a.gu: Cut-off (OFF) અને saturation (ON).

q.en: What is V_CE when the transistor switch is ON?
q.gu: Transistor switch ON હોય ત્યારે V_CE કેટલો હોય?

a.en: About 0.2 V (V_CE(sat)).
a.gu: આશરે 0.2 V (V_CE(sat)).

q.en: What is V_CE when the switch is OFF?
q.gu: Switch OFF હોય ત્યારે V_CE કેટલો હોય?

a.en: Almost equal to V_CC.
a.gu: લગભગ V_CC જેટલો.

q.en: What is the condition for saturation?
q.gu: Saturation માટેની શરત શું છે?

a.en: I_B > I_C(sat) / β.
a.gu: I_B > I_C(sat) / β.

q.en: What is a DC load line?
q.gu: DC load line એટલે શું?

a.en: A straight line on output characteristics given by V_CE = V_CC − I_C R_C; the Q-point lies on it.
a.gu: Output characteristics પર V_CE = V_CC − I_C R_C થી મળતી સીધી રેખા; Q-point તેના પર હોય છે.

q.en: Which logic gate does a transistor switch act as?
q.gu: Transistor switch કયા logic gate તરીકે કામ કરે છે?

a.en: NOT gate (inverter).
a.gu: NOT gate (inverter).

q.en: Why is a diode connected across a relay coil?
q.gu: Relay coil પર diode કેમ જોડાય છે?

a.en: To absorb the back EMF and protect the transistor (freewheeling diode).
a.gu: Back EMF શોષી transistor ને રક્ષણ આપવા (freewheeling diode).
